issues.title: Logger uses direct logging.getLogger initialization
issues.description: The rule requires logger instances to be created using the pattern `logger: "logging.Logger" = get_logger("module_name")` from prefect.logging, but the code uses the direct `logging.getLogger(__name__)` pattern instead.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
# Logger for SDK fetcher operations
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
issues.rule_name: Logger Instances Must Follow Standard Initialization Pattern

issues.title: Incorrect deployment filtering breaks full-name matching
issues.description: The deployment filtering logic checks `dep.name not in deployment_names` instead of checking `full_name not in deployment_names`. This causes the filter to incorrectly evaluate when users specify deployment names in 'flow-name/deployment-name' format. When a user provides a full deployment name like 'my-flow/production', the code checks if 'production' (the short name) is in the list containing 'my-flow/production', which fails, causing the deployment to enter the fallback matching logic unnecessarily. This breaks the fast-path check and could lead to incorrect filtering behavior where deployments are included or excluded inappropriately.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
# If filtering by deployment name, check the full name matches
        full_name = f"{flow_name}/{dep.name}"
        if deployment_names and dep.name not in deployment_names:
            # Only include if the full name matches (filter was by name parts)
            # Skip if user specified full names and this doesn't match
            found_match = False

issues.title: Missing type validation for work pool job variables schema
issues.description: The code removes the `isinstance(variables, dict)` type check before assigning `base_job_template["variables"]` to `job_vars_schema`. The `job_vars_schema` variable is typed as `dict[str, Any]` and is expected to be a dictionary throughout the SDK generation process. If `base_job_template["variables"]` contains a non-dict value (like a list, string, or other type due to malformed work pool configuration), this will cause type inconsistencies that could lead to runtime errors in downstream code that expects a dict, such as the template renderer or SDK generator that processes the schema.

issues.title: Removed strict zip validation enables silent data corruption
issues.description: The code removes `strict=True` from the `zip(pool_names_list, results)` call in the work pool parallel fetching logic. The strict parameter ensures that both iterables have the same length and raises a ValueError if they don't match. Without it, if there's a mismatch between the number of work pool names and the results from `asyncio.gather()` (which should never happen in correct code but could occur due to bugs in the async gather logic or unexpected exceptions), the zip will silently truncate to the shorter sequence. This means some work pool results could be dropped or mismatched with the wrong names, leading to incorrect work pool metadata in the generated SDK without any warning or error.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #20241 - Add documentation for prefect sdk generate CLI

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds two docs pages for the beta `prefect sdk generate` command: an auto-generated CLI reference (`docs/v3/api-ref/cli/sdk.mdx`) and a how-to guide (`docs/v3/advanced/generate-custom-sdk.mdx`), wired into `docs/docs.json`. It also makes four small behavioral edits in `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py`: a debug log line, removal of a work-pool `variables` guard, removal of `zip(strict=True)`, and a change to how bare deployment names are matched against the filter.

The docs are largely consistent with the code. The CLI reference matches the Typer help text and options, the template methods (`with_options`, `with_infra`, `run`, `run_async`) match what the guide describes, and the nav JSON parses. The async example is wrong, though: `PrefectFlowRunFuture.result()` is synchronous, so `await future.result()` fails at runtime. The fetcher edits are the bigger concern. The filter change silently drops the ambiguous short-name warning, and an existing test asserts that warning. I reproduced this against the head commit with a mocked client: `deployment_names=["production"]` now yields no warning, while the base logic emits one. The PR adds no tests for any of the four fetcher changes, and the project's ruff config flags the new logger placement as E402.

This should not merge as-is. The docs fix is one line, and the filter change should be reverted, since the original full-name comparison was already correct.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Two correctness regressions block merge. The fetcher filter change drops the ambiguous short-name warning, which the existing test `test_fetch_sdk_data_ambiguous_short_name_warning` asserts. I could not run that test because its fixture needs a hosted Prefect API, but I reproduced the behavior with a mocked client. The async docs example awaits a synchronous method. The remaining items are lint and defensive-check removals that should be reverted or justified.

architecture.overview: `prefect sdk generate` (src/prefect/cli/sdk.py) calls `generate_sdk` in src/prefect/_sdk/generator.py. That calls `fetch_sdk_data` in src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py, which reads deployments, flows and work pools from the Prefect API through `PrefectClient`. The data is converted into models in `_sdk/models.py`. `renderer.py` turns work-pool job-variable schemas into fields, and the `sdk.py.jinja` template renders everything into a single typed Python module. The generated module exposes a `deployments.from_name()` handle with `run`, `run_async`, `with_options` and `with_infra`, backed by `PrefectFlowRunFuture`. This PR adds no runtime components. It adds user-facing documentation for that pipeline and makes four edits inside the fetcher. The deployment-name filter change is the one that alters behavior in a way that matters.
steps: Entry point: `prefect sdk generate` in src/prefect/cli/sdk.py parses `--output`, `--flow` and `--deployment`, then calls `generate_sdk`.

Fetch: `fetch_sdk_data` in src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py checks auth, applies server-side name filters, groups deployments by flow, and fetches work pools in parallel. This PR changes the deployment-name matching around line 397 and removes a guard around line 182.
Render: `renderer.py` reads each work pool's `job_variables_schema` to build `with_infra()` fields. That schema now flows through unguarded, so a malformed template would reach `.get()` directly.

Generated output: `sdk.py.jinja` emits `deployments.from_name()`, which returns a deployment handle. Its `run()` returns a `PrefectFlowRunFuture`, and its `run_async()` is a coroutine that returns the same type. The new guide documents this surface.
Docs: `generate-custom-sdk.mdx` is a how-to guide, and `sdk.mdx` is the auto-generated CLI reference. Both are registered in `docs/docs.json`, and `form-building` moves into a new Deployments group.

findings.title: Ambiguous short-name warning silently dropped by deployment filter change
findings.body:
The filter check changed from `full_name not in deployment_names` to `dep.name not in deployment_names`. The original line was already correct for full `flow/deployment` filters. The new line changes behavior only for bare names. When a user passes `--deployment production` and two flows each have a `production` deployment, `dep.name` is in the list, so the whole matching block is skipped. That skips the `short_name_matches` bookkeeping, and the "Short deployment name ... matched N deployments" warning is never emitted.

I reproduced this against head with a mocked client (two `production` deployments under `etl-flow` and `sync-flow`, filter `["production"]`). Both deployments are included, but the warning list is empty. The existing test `test_fetch_sdk_data_ambiguous_short_name_warning` in `tests/_sdk/test_fetcher.py` asserts that exact warning, so it will fail. I could not run the test here because its fixture requires a hosted Prefect API.

::diff{file="src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py" lines="395-399"}

Revert to the original `full_name not in deployment_names` comparison. The PR does not need this change to support full-name filters.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py` around line 397, the condition `if deployment_names and dep.name not in deployment_names:` was changed from comparing `full_name`. Revert it to compare `full_name` against `deployment_names`. This restores the short-name ambiguity tracking (`short_name_matches`) that emits the "Short deployment name ... matched N deployments" warning, which `test_fetch_sdk_data_ambiguous_short_name_warning` in `tests/_sdk/test_fetcher.py` asserts. Full-name filters like `flow/deployment` already work with the original comparison. Do not change the matching loop below it.

findings.title: Docs example awaits a synchronous `result()` method
findings.body:
In the async example, the guide does `result = await future.result()`. `PrefectFlowRunFuture.result()` in `src/prefect/futures.py` is synchronous. It calls `run_coro_as_sync(self.aresult(...))` and returns the flow's return value `R`. Awaiting that return value raises `TypeError`, or the value is not awaitable at all. Readers who copy this snippet will get a crash.

The awaitable variant is `aresult()`, which the generated template's `PrefectFlowRunFuture` provides.

::code{file="docs/v3/advanced/generate-custom-sdk.mdx" lines="124-136"}

Change the example to `result = await future.aresult()`. Keep the sync example elsewhere on the page using `.result()`.
findings.fixPrompt: In `docs/v3/advanced/generate-custom-sdk.mdx` at line 132, the async example in the "Async usage" section calls `await future.result()`. `PrefectFlowRunFuture.result()` in `src/prefect/futures.py` is synchronous, so this line raises a TypeError. Change it to `await future.aresult()`, which is the awaitable variant defined on the same class. Leave the other synchronous examples on the page unchanged.

findings.title: Logger assignment inserted between import blocks triggers E402
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py`, the line `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` (around line 20) sits between `import prefect` and the `from prefect._sdk.models import (...)` block. That makes the remaining imports non-top-level and triggers ruff E402 and import-sort (I001) failures. Move the logger definition below the full import section, just before the first top-level code (after the `if TYPE_CHECKING:` import block), so all imports stay at the top. Verify with `ruff check src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py`.

findings.title: Removed isinstance guard lets a non-dict `variables` reach the renderer
findings.body:
The PR replaced the `if isinstance(variables, dict): job_vars_schema = variables` guard with a plain assignment. Nothing in the diff explains this. If a work pool's `base_job_template["variables"]` is ever a non-dict (for example a list or string from a hand-edited template), `WorkPoolInfo.job_variables_schema` now holds that value. `renderer.py` line 271 then calls `schema.get("properties")`, which raises `AttributeError` and aborts generation for every deployment, not just the one using that pool. The old guard defaulted the value to `{}`, which the renderer already treats as "no fields".

This input is unlikely, but the guard was defensive and the PR removes it without a test or a reason.

::diff{file="src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py" lines="178-183"}

Restore the isinstance check, or explicitly coerce non-dict values to `{}`.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py` around lines 180-182 (`_fetch_work_pool`), the `isinstance(variables, dict)` guard was removed, so `job_vars_schema` may now hold a non-dict value from `base_job_template["variables"]`. `src/prefect/_sdk/renderer.py` line 271 calls `schema.get(...)` on it, which would crash generation. Restore the guard so that only dict values are assigned to `job_vars_schema`, and otherwise leave it as `{}`. Add a unit test in `tests/_sdk/test_fetcher.py` covering a non-dict `variables` value.

findings.title: Dropped `zip(strict=True)` removes a length-mismatch check
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py` at line 220 (`_fetch_work_pools_parallel`), the `zip(pool_names_list, results)` call had `strict=True` removed. Restore `strict=True`. The project requires Python >=3.10, so the argument is supported. Both sequences are built from the same set, so the strict check should never fail, but it guards against silent truncation if that changes.

findings.title: Generated CLI reference and nav are consistent with the Typer command
findings.body: The auto-generated `sdk.mdx` matches `src/prefect/cli/sdk.py`: the `generate` command help, examples, and the `--output`, `--flow`, and `--deployment` options all agree. It follows the same conventions as the existing generated CLI pages, including the `title: " "` and `\$` escapes seen in `init.mdx` and `block.mdx`. `docs/docs.json` parses as valid JSON, and the new `v3/api-ref/cli/sdk` entry is in alphabetical order. The guide's `with_options` and `with_infra` option names match `sdk.py.jinja`, and the link targets exist under `docs/v3/how-to-guides/deployments/`.

findings.title: Full flow/deployment filters select the right deployment
findings.body: Using full `flow/deployment` names as filters works correctly on the base logic and on head. The full-name comparison selects only the matching flow's deployment, which is what the new guide recommends for precise filtering. The problem is limited to the bare-name path described in the high-severity finding.
